full_judgment:
2. The present appellant, as plaintiff, filed the above mentioned Title Suit No. 33 of 1992 for recovery of khas possessions of the "Ga" schedule property by evicting the defendants there from. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that 50 decimals land of plot Nos.526 to 530 of S.A. Khatian No. 463 of mouza Amanatganj Originally belonged to Ganoda Sundari and Lalit Kumar. The said Ganoda Sundari and Lalit Kumar died in the year 1948 and their heirs used to possess the same. That for arrears of rent the said property was sold in auction in a certificate proceeding bearing No. 2350/1957-58 and one Sahera Khatun, Araj Ali Sikder, Abdus Salam and Azizur Rahman purchased the same in auction on 23.11.1957 and got possession through court on 03.11.1960 and since then they had been possessing the same on payment of rent after mutating their names in the Government sheresta. That the auction purchasers filed a partition suit being numbered Title Suit No. 89 of 1967 among themselves and got their shares partitioned. Subsequently, the plaintiff purchased 12½ decimals of land from Azizur Rahman by registered deed dated 10.07.1968. The plaintiff also entered into a contract to purchase the share of Abdus Salam. Since Abdus Salam subsequently denied to execute the kabala deed as per that contract the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 428 of 1974 for specific performance of contract in the name of the defendant No. 1-his benamder and got decree and thereafter Abdus . Salam executed the kabala deed in the name of the defendant No. 1 Azaharuddin. The further case of the plaintiffs was that the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 2 to 4, namely, Mainuddin, Abdul Jabbar Ali and Abu Sufian Mia in collusion with the local administration and for the purpose of creating title, obtained a decree on the basis of a false rent suit in the name of Mothahar Hossain the brother-in-law of Abdul Jabbar Mia for which the auction purchasers along with Azaharuddin filed Title Suit No. 762 of 1975 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Barisal for declaration against the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos.2 to 4 and that suit was decreed on 17.05.1976. Thereafter the auction purchaser Sharea Khatun and the plaintiff’s benamder Azharuddin Molla applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal for giving them possession after evicting the allottees there from. The Deputy Commissioner, Barisal then filed Title Suit No. 343 of 1977 for cancellation of the decree dated 17.05.1976 passed in Title Suit No. 762 of 1975, but that suit subsequently abated. The Deputy Commissioner then passed orders for de-requisition of the house in Case Nos. 54 of 1948 and 60 of 1948 in the year 1987. That the defendant Nos. 2 to 4 being not allottees prayed for allotment after declaring the suit property as enemy property to continue with their illegal and unauthorized occupation but, no order was passed to that effect. The further case of the plaintiff was that after the death of Araj Ali Sikder, his heirs denied the plaintiffs title and for which the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 143 of 1983 and got decree. Thus the plaintiff has got right, tile and interest over the suit land. But since the defendants denied to hand over possession of the suit property to the plaintiff lastly on 18.11.1988 the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary produced by the contesting parties, arrived at a finding that the plaintiff failed to prove the alleged auction sale of the suit property and also that the suit was barred by limitation and accordingly dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiff was not entitled to get the decree of khash possession. 

 8. Mr. M.A. Salam, the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant has advanced his submission on the grounds on which leave was granted. The learned Counsel has submitted that the courts below dismissed the suit mainly on the finding that the plaintiff could not prove the alleged auction sale of the suit property by adducing necessary documents, but did not consider at all that the plaintiff filed an application before the appellate court below praying for adducing additional evidence in order to prove that auction sale but the appellate court below did not consider the said application at all; that the High Court Division did not take into consideration this fact of non consideration of the plaintiff's application for additional evidence by the appellate court below. The learned Counsel has argued that serious injustice was committed to the plaintiff dismissing his suit on the ground that the plaintiff could not adduce necessary evidence for proving the alleged auction sale of the suit property. The learned Counsel has argued that where the plaintiff filed an application before the appellate court below praying for adducing necessary documentary evidence to prove the alleged auction sale of the suit property, he ought to have been given an opportunity for adducing those necessary evidence in order to prove his case, but the courts below without giving him that opportunity arrived at the decision that the plaintiff could not prove his case by adducing necessary evidence and thus committed not only injustice to the plaintiff but also error of law. The learned Counsel for the appellant has argued also that the appellate court below committed wrong also in holding that the suit for khash possession was not maintainable without a prayer for declaration of title ignoring the fact that the plaintiff already got his title in the suit property declared by the decree passed in Title Suit No. 762 of 1975 and that decree still holds good. The learned Counsel has contended that since the plaintiff earlier filed the above Title Suit No. 762 of 1975 praying for declaration of his title in the suit land and got decree in that suit and since the said decree is still subsisting the plaintiff did not require at all to pray for declaration of his title in the suit land. 

 9. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Senior Counsel who has appeared for the contesting respondent has made submission supporting the impugned judgment of the High Court Division as well as those of the courts below. The learned Counsel for the contesting respondents has argued that all the courts below have scrutinized and considered the evidence adduced by both the contesting parties and rightly arrived at concurrent findings that the plaintiff could not prove his case at all and that the alleged auction purchasers never got possession of the suit land and the suit was barred by limitation and in the circumstances the plaintiff was not entitled to get a decree for khash possession. 

 12. We do not find any reason for not agreeing with the above concurrent findings of all the three courts below. In the present appeal before this Division though it was submitted from the side of the plaintiff that the lower appellate court did not consider at all the plaintiffs application for additional evidence and thus a miscarriage of justice has been committed. But considering the facts and circumstances we do not find this argument from the side of the appellant important at all. It has already been pointed out above that the courts below opined to the effect that the alleged auction purchasers alleged right, title and interest in the suit land, if any, extinguished by lapse of time since they could not acquire possession of the suit land by virtue of their alleged auction purchase. So, in the circumstances the non-consideration of the plaintiff’s application for adducing additional evidence for proving that alleged auction sale of the suit property does not matter at all. The courts below, accepting the plaintiffs case of auction sale of the suit property, found that the alleged auction purchasers alleged right, title and interest in the suit property extinguished by lapse of time since they could not get possession of the suit property at all. So, in the circumstances the non-consideration of plaintiff’s application for adducing additional evidence cannot be a ground for allowing this appeal. The other ground of the appellant that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 762 of 1975 declaring plaintiffs title in the suit land still holds good and as such plaintiff is entitled to get khas possession of the suit land also is not acceptable in the present facts and circumstances of the case. In this case it has been proved that neither the plaintiff nor his predecessors-in-interest the alleged auction purchasers ever got possession of the suit land and as such plaintiffs alleged title in the suit land even if declared by a court long ago-long more than 12 years before filing this suit by him extinguished.
